rule: Direct exposure records name only objectives whose demand is tested. Unresolved or context-only links are retained in mapping_exceptions.json and excluded from direct objective exposure; all original paper parts remain in paper_evidence.json.

2023/P2/2(c).note: PDF pp.3–4 asks for pesticide uptake into roots. Neither figure nor an available mark scheme determines the intended uptake process. Translocation in phloem and osmosis/water uptake are contextual links, not confirmed credited demands. No direct objective exposure assigned; do not infer pesticide entry by osmosis.

explain how light intensity affects the rate of transpiration
2023/P3/1(c)(ii).note: Balancing water absorption against loss is answered through the factors that change transpiration (shade, cooler place) or watering; re-mapped to the factor objectives.

2025/P2/2(a)(ii).note: PDF p.4 inspected: vessel wall/lumen provide plausible evidence for vein structure. Retain medium confidence; the absence of a mark scheme limits certainty about the expected feature. The actual figure, rather than the topic alone, supports the mapping.

objective_starts: describe the structure of a palisade cell and a liver cell
2024/P2/6(a).note: Codex inspected the complete figure on PDF p.11: Q points to the nucleus. This part tests cell-structure identification, not drawing/interpreting prepared meiosis slides. OBJ-6116-3.2-01 is the closest explicit cell-structure objective; the diagram is a dividing animal cell, not the specific palisade/liver exemplars named there.

2022/P2/1(d)(i).note: PDF p.3 asks for the meaning of extinction. No objective explicitly defines it. Keep glossary support and conservation context, but do not credit habitat-destruction causes as examined by this definition part. Confidence is in this exclusion decision, not in a direct mapping.
